Rent Review Program — City of Fremont

About

The Rent Review Program helps tenants and landlords resolve concerns about rent increases. If a landlord in Fremont proposes a rent increase of more than 5% within any 12-month period, the tenant can request a review and, if needed, a formal hearing. This applies to all residential rentals in Fremont, including single-family homes.

Background

On October 3, 2017, the Fremont City Council adopted the Rent Review Ordinance, effective January 1, 2018. The ordinance covers all residential rental units in Fremont, including single family homes.

How the Program Works

On November 18, 2025, the City Council adopted the FY 2025/2026 Rent Review Program fee of $23 per unit for landlords. On February 18, 2020, the City Council amended the Rent Review Ordinance so that landlords who own less than 5 rental units in Fremont are exempt from the fee.

New rent increase notice requirements: all rent increases must be in writing; show the contact information of the landlord or responsible party; if the increase is over 5%, include an explanation of why the increase is needed; and include the Rent Review Noticing Form.

To initiate the Rent Review Process, complete the Request for Rent Review form and submit it via email, mail, or in person along with a copy of the Rent Increase Notice. A request must be made within 15 calendar days from the date on the Rent Increase Notice. Once a request form is received, the office will contact the opposing party and request that they complete the Response to Review Form within 5 business days, or else the Rent Increase Notice is invalid. If a landlord does not want to participate themselves, they may designate a responsible party with authority to adjust rents and resolve disputes.

The purpose of the Rent Review Board is to evaluate the reasonableness of proposed rent increases at the request of either a landlord or tenant. Requests for a Rent Review Board hearing may be made if a proposed rent increase is over 5%, and if no agreement was made during consultation and mediation. Hearings are publicly noticed and open to the public.

Contact: Landlord-Tenant Services 510-574-2270; Billing Questions 510-494-4790; Rent Review Program, 3300 Capitol Ave., Building B, Fremont, CA 94538; 510-733-4945; RentReview@Fremont.gov.

Frequently asked questions: The Ordinance does not prevent a landlord from raising rent by any amount; however, increases over 5% must include the reason and are subject to a Rent Review Board hearing. Landlords are not required to file copies of rent increase notices with the City. The Ordinance covers any housing unit offered for rent in Fremont, including single-family homes and mobile homes (mobile homes only for the unit itself, not the pad, which is under FMC Chapter 9.55). Anyone may request a rent review by emailing rentreview@fremont.gov or calling the Rent Review Hotline at (510) 733-4945. Participation is mandatory: failure of a landlord to appear and participate in good faith voids the rent increase notice; failure of a tenant to participate terminates the Ordinance's services for that tenant and makes the increase effective as noticed. A representative may participate only with legal authority via a responsible party declaration. On landlord retaliation: the California Department of Consumer Affairs defines retaliatory eviction or action as a landlord raising rent, seeking eviction, or otherwise punishing a tenant for asserting legal tenant rights; Bay Area Legal Aid's advice line is (800) 551-5554.

Rent Review Process — City of Fremont

A tenant challenging a rent increase is first encouraged to reach out to their housing provider directly. If no agreement is reached, the first step is consultation, which may include mediation. If the dispute is not resolved through consultation and/or mediation, either a landlord or a tenant may ask for a hearing before a Rent Review Board if the proposed rent increase is over 5%.

Both landlords and tenants are required to participate in the process at no charge to the participants. While the recommendations of the Rent Review Board are not binding, the City believes that a neutral setting led by a trained Rent Review Board will result in fair and equitable resolutions.

A request to initiate the process must be made within 15 calendar days from the date on the Rent Increase Notice, submitted via email, mail, or in person with a copy of the notice. The opposing party must submit the Response to Rent Review form within 5 business days, or the Rent Increase Notice is invalid.
